240: FULL can also reduce idle processing load
241: FULL / ECO works separately from the automatic silence sleep on the next page. FULL retains analysis capability; both modes can suspend the main audio processing once playback is stopped, all inputs are zero and internal state has settled.
242: Silence sleep after stopping, and waking up
243: The wait is before sleep. Playback or incoming signal restores processing in the current audio block.
245: When the host reports stopped playback and all inputs, including main and sidechain, are zero, the plugin continues processing pending delay, filter tails and TP recovery. Only after these settle does it skip the main oversampling and Ceiling work that has no remaining audio to process.
246: A quiet sound alone does not trigger sleep, and pressing Stop does not immediately cut off processing. Live input, sidechain, tails or parameter changes keep normal processing active. Processing also continues if the host supplies no reliable transport state.
251: Normal processing resumes in the current audio block.
252: Any nonzero sample arrives at main or sidechain input
253: Processing resumes in that block, even if the host still reports stopped.
255: Processes the current state again, then checks whether subsequent blocks qualify for sleep.
257: Normal processing continues. An all-zero passage alone does not trigger stopped-transport sleep.
258: The first block containing sound is not skipped
259: Input is checked across the current block before deciding whether to skip processing. Required state is retained before sleep, and waking adds no extra waiting period. Existing Lookahead, oversampling latency and host compensation still apply at the current settings.
261: Offline rendering also follows transport state and each block's input. A block containing nonzero material is processed immediately, without relying on editor timer updates. Export alignment still depends on the host's rendering and latency-compensation process.
262: Load may fall some time after Stop, especially with deep limiting or SMOOTH. ASIO-Guard reflects the host's overall scheduling and is also affected by other plugins, routing and buffer settings. A reduction in one plugin's processing time cannot be converted directly into a percentage on that meter.
